Stubbles, J. (2000). Energy Use in the U.S. Steel Industry: An Historical Perspective and Future Opportunities. Prepared under contract to Energetics, Inc. for the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies, Washington, DC, September 2000.

Report of 31 printed pages plus front matter (58 PDF pages). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (running footer "Energy Use in the U.S. Steel Industry N"). Units are U.S.: per short (net) ton, MBtu, scf, lb; kept as reported. TRAP: every MBtu total in the report counts electricity at 10,500 Btu/kWh (primary, 100% coal-based), so mixed-carrier totals are NOT loaded as final energy (other-values); electricity is loaded in kWh and fuels in their own units. Coke and injectant rates printed as kg/NTHM are mass ratios. Loaded: good-practice pellet, sinter and coke plant energy (Bouman 1983 and IISI 1998 reprints), BF Table 2, alternate ironmaking Table 4 (per metric ton, with capital $/t), Iron Dynamics RHF+SAF Table 11, BOF Table 5, EAF Table 6, reheating and rolling, COREX fuel rate. Adjacent to IISI 1998 (Energy use in the steel industry, not held): Stubbles reprints its pellet and sinter figures. No price year printed (2000 assumed).
